title: Segmentation-driven heuristic scorer for per-customer & per-route batch/cache safe-push
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We need an automated but safe system that recommends and applies per-customer and per-route batching/caching profiles. Current manual tuning is labor intensive and brittle: different customers and routes have very different latency/cost trade-offs. Goal: ship a heuristic-based scorer that synthesizes segmentation signals (customer tiers, historical latency, token distribution), allowlist/denylist constraints, and stability heuristics to produce ranked configuration candidates and a safe apply/rollback workflow. Scope: (1) offline scoring and simulation on historical traces, (2) runtime scoring API that returns ranked profiles and a confidence score, (3) safe-canary apply with automated health checks and rollback triggers.
updates: 2025-02-12 - Maya Chen: Kickoff. Collected sample traces for top 25 customers and 50 highest-traffic routes. Initial scoring rubric drafted.

2025-02-18 - Diego Ramirez: Prototype scorer implemented (alpha) that computes expected token-level cost delta and cache hit potential. Ran replay on 10-day window; median estimated savings 12% for high-throughput routes.

2025-02-22 - Priya Patel (PM): Product constraints: allowlist required for any profile that enables quantized models; enterprise customers must be opt-in. Added label requirements to scoring pipeline.

2025-02-26 - Design review (Alex Kim): UX for Console recommendations: show confidence score, estimated savings, and one-click preview of rollout plan. Design provided wireframes (link in attachments).

2025-03-03 - Diego Ramirez: Canary workflow implemented: shadow replay, 1% production traffic canary, and automated rollback on any of three thresholds (latency regression > 15pct, error rate increase > 0.5pct absolute, quality regression flagged by evalhook).
acceptance_criteria: Offline scoring produces stable ranking across 14-day and 30-day windows (rank correlation > 0.85) for sampled customers
Scoring API returns top 3 candidate profiles with estimated monthly token-cost delta and confidence score
Console displays recommendation card with confidence, estimated savings, and links to simulation artifacts
Canary rollout supports: shadow replay validation, 1/5/25/100% staged rollout, automated rollback based on observability rules
Automated rollback triggers are tested in chaos/rollback tests and succeed within configured SLOs
technical_notes: Scorer inputs: per-route token histogram, peak QPS, median latency, recent cache hit rate, customer tier, allowlist/denylist flags, historical quality regression flags

Heuristic components: cost_delta_estimator (modeling batching/caching effect on per-token cost), stability_score (variance of latency and error rate), quality_risk_score (based on eval regressions and model variant change), policy_constraints (allowlist/denylist, enterprise opt-in)
Ranking formula (high level): rank_score = weight_cost * expected_savings - weight_risk * quality_risk_score + weight_stability * stability_score - policy_penalty
We will train weights via grid search against historical replays to maximize realized savings subject to quality_regression_rate < 0.5pct for production customers
Runtime API returns a JSON blob (flat) with candidate profiles, confidence percent, and sandbox_link for preview. No sensitive data included in response.
qa_plan: Unit tests for cost_delta_estimator with synthetic token distributions
Integration test: replay 10-day production trace in staging and compare projections vs actual when applying profile in a controlled rollout
Chaos test: induce a simulated model quality regression in canary; verify rollback completes and traffic returns to baseline
E2E: Console recommendation -> apply -> monitor -> rollback path exercised by QA
